result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.min_cost_flow()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute minimum cost flow from source to sink. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L21096-L21254){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.min_cost_flow( source, sink, demand=None, capacity=None, cost=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Finds the flow that minimizes total cost. Can either send a specified amount of flow (demand) or find the maximum flow at minimum cost. Uses the Successive Shortest Path algorithm with Bellman-Ford, which handles negative edge costs correctly. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Source node (integer ID or string label). [sink]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Sink node (integer ID or string label). [demand]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Required flow amount. If `None` (default), finds maximum flow at minimum cost. If specified, the algorithm attempts to send exactly this much flow. [capacity]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional name of edge attribute to use as capacity. If `None` (default), uses edge weights for weighted graphs, or `1.0` for unweighted graphs. [cost]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional name of edge attribute to use as cost per unit flow. If `None` (default), looks for a `"cost"` attribute; otherwise uses `1.0`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [tuple[float, float, dict[int, float]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A tuple containing: (1) total_flow, the total amount of flow sent, (2) total_cost: the total cost of the flow, and (3) flow_dict, a dictionary mapping `edge_id` to flow amount for edges with positive flow. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is undirected, source/sink doesn't exist, they're the same node, demand is negative, or demand cannot be satisfied. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - graph must be directed (use `.to_directed()` to convert if needed) - self-loops are ignored in flow computation - negative costs are allowed (the algorithm handles them correctly) - the algorithm uses Successive Shortest Path with Bellman-Ford, with time complexity `O(V * E * F)` where `F` is the total flow ## Examples {.doc-examples} With two possible paths from `S` to `T`, the algorithm prefers the cheaper route through `A` (per-unit cost 2) over the more expensive one through `B` (per-unit cost 3), only using the second path once the first path's capacity is saturated: ::: {#0895ecd2 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True, weighted=True) .add_node(label="S") .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="T") .add_edge("S", "A", weight=10.0, cost=1.0) # capacity 10, cost 1 .add_edge("S", "B", weight=10.0, cost=2.0) # capacity 10, cost 2 .add_edge("A", "T", weight=10.0, cost=1.0) # capacity 10, cost 1 .add_edge("B", "T", weight=10.0, cost=1.0) # capacity 10, cost 1 ) total_flow, total_cost, flow_dict = graph.min_cost_flow("S", "T") # Returns (20.0, 50.0): both paths get used once the cheaper one saturates (total_flow, total_cost) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (20.0, 50.0) ``` ::: ::: Passing `demand` sends exactly that much flow (rather than the maximum possible), which is useful when you have a fixed requirement to satisfy at minimum cost: ::: {#3a1e2f8d .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True, weighted=True) .add_node(label="S") .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="T") .add_edge("S", "A", weight=20.0, cost=5.0) .add_edge("A", "T", weight=20.0, cost=3.0) ) # Send exactly 10 units of flow total_flow, total_cost, flow_dict = graph.min_cost_flow("S", "T", demand=10.0) # Returns (10.0, 80.0): 10 units at a combined per-unit cost of 8 (total_flow, total_cost) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (10.0, 80.0) ``` ::: ::: Just like `max_flow()`, you can use custom attributes for both capacity and cost instead of the defaults: ::: {#97c2817a .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B", bandwidth=100, price=5) .add_edge("B", "C", bandwidth=50, price=3) .add_edge("A", "C", bandwidth=30, price=10) ) total_flow, total_cost, flow_dict = graph.min_cost_flow( "A", "C", capacity="bandwidth", cost="price" ) (total_flow, total_cost) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (80.0, 700.0) ``` ::: ::: This scales naturally to classic transportation problems, like shipping from warehouses to stores at minimum total cost: ::: {#a708e5f3 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True, weighted=True) .add_node(label="Source") .add_node(label="W1") # Warehouse 1 .add_node(label="W2") # Warehouse 2 .add_node(label="S1") # Store 1 .add_node(label="S2") # Store 2 .add_node(label="Sink") # Source to warehouses (supply) .add_edge("Source", "W1", weight=50.0, cost=0.0) .add_edge("Source", "W2", weight=60.0, cost=0.0) # Warehouses to stores (shipping costs) .add_edge("W1", "S1", weight=100.0, cost=8.0) .add_edge("W1", "S2", weight=100.0, cost=5.0) .add_edge("W2", "S1", weight=100.0, cost=4.0) .add_edge("W2", "S2", weight=100.0, cost=7.0) # Stores to sink (demand) .add_edge("S1", "Sink", weight=40.0, cost=0.0) .add_edge("S2", "Sink", weight=50.0, cost=0.0) ) flow, cost, assignment = graph.min_cost_flow("Source", "Sink", demand=90.0) # Total shipping cost for meeting the 90-unit demand cost ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` 410.0 ``` ::: :::
